metadata.title: Cobimetinib and Vemurafenib Therapy
metadata.indication: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

supplemental_source_documents.section: Current EMA product information supplement, component-specific
Current EMA product information supplement, component-specific

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or the specialist authority specified in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: All modifications require consultant/pharmacy review. Component-specific advice and dose levels are reference text, never an automatically calculated prescription. Missing values remain unassessed.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding derived from NCCP 00373 Version 3. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

source_conflicts.resolution: Exactly 60 ms change is not covered by the printed <60 and >60 rows. Withhold and seek consultant interpretation.
The printed <10-point recovery criterion overlaps the <40% permanent-stop criterion. Keep withheld and require specialist interpretation when both apply.

removed_unsupported_generic_rules: Legacy shared whole-regimen QT/LVEF/CK/ILD/haemorrhage shortcuts were replaced only where a source-specific pathway exists. Named symptoms without source dose criteria prompt assessment, not invented thresholds.

indications.description: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.

treatment.schedule_summary: Cobimetinib once daily on days 1–21 followed by a 7-day break; vemurafenib twice daily continuously. Repeat every 28 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
treatment.cycle_convention_note: 28-day cycle: cobimetinib days 1–21 then seven days off; vemurafenib continues every day including days 22–28.

administration.note: Days 1–21, then a seven-day cobimetinib break.
Continuous, including days 22–28. Avoid routinely taking both daily doses on an empty stomach.

action.message: QTc >500 ms at baseline: vemurafenib treatment is not recommended.

rules.explanation: QTc >500 ms at baseline: vemurafenib treatment is not recommended.

action.message: QTc >500 ms requires interruption of vemurafenib and review of baseline change and prior occurrences. Correct reversible causes; resumption requires QTc strictly <500 ms. No cobimetinib dose modification is required for this QT finding alone.

rules.explanation: QTc >500 ms requires interruption of vemurafenib and review of baseline change and prior occurrences. Correct reversible causes; resumption requires QTc strictly <500 ms. No cobimetinib dose modification is required for this QT finding alone.

action.message: QTc >500 ms AND increase >60 ms from pretreatment: permanently discontinue vemurafenib.

rules.explanation: QTc >500 ms AND increase >60 ms from pretreatment: permanently discontinue vemurafenib.

action.message: An episode with QTc >500 ms and >60 ms increase requires permanent discontinuation even if the current QTc has recovered.

rules.explanation: An episode with QTc >500 ms and >60 ms increase requires permanent discontinuation even if the current QTc has recovered.

action.message: SOURCE BOUNDARY GAP: the NCCP table specifies >60 ms for permanent cessation and <60 ms for the interruption/reduction rows; exactly 60 ms is not allocated. Keep vemurafenib withheld and obtain specialist interpretation; do not automatically restart or invent a permanent-stop boundary.

rules.explanation: SOURCE BOUNDARY GAP: the NCCP table specifies >60 ms for permanent cessation and <60 ms for the interruption/reduction rows; exactly 60 ms is not allocated. Keep vemurafenib withheld and obtain specialist interpretation; do not automatically restart or invent a permanent-stop boundary.

action.message: Record the actual pretreatment QTc before classifying the >60 ms change; current QTc >500 ms still independently requires interruption.

rules.explanation: Record the actual pretreatment QTc before classifying the >60 ms change; current QTc >500 ms still independently requires interruption.

action.message: Record first, second or third QTc >500 ms occurrence; recurrence changes the reduction/permanent-stop pathway.

rules.explanation: Record first, second or third QTc >500 ms occurrence; recurrence changes the reduction/permanent-stop pathway.

action.message: First occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg twice daily if already reduced. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

rules.explanation: First occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg twice daily if already reduced. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

action.message: Second occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 480 mg twice daily, or permanent discontinuation if already at 480 mg twice daily. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

rules.explanation: Second occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 480 mg twice daily, or permanent discontinuation if already at 480 mg twice daily. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

action.message: Third QTc >500 ms occurrence requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation; later QT recovery does not remove the stop history.

rules.explanation: Third QTc >500 ms occurrence requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation; later QT recovery does not remove the stop history.

action.message: Second QT episode when vemurafenib is already reduced to 480 mg twice daily: permanently discontinue.

rules.explanation: Second QT episode when vemurafenib is already reduced to 480 mg twice daily: permanently discontinue.

action.message: Do not restart at QTc 500 ms: the source recovery threshold is strictly <500 ms.

rules.explanation: Do not restart at QTc 500 ms: the source recovery threshold is strictly <500 ms.

action.message: Severe vemurafenib hypersensitivity requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Severe vemurafenib hypersensitivity requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: A severe dermatological reaction, including SJS/TEN/DRESS, requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation. This overrides the generic first-grade4 consultant-choice row.

action.message: Other intolerable grade 2 or grade 3 toxicity: interrupt until grade 0–1. First event: reference restart 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg if already reduced. Second event: 480 mg twice daily, or stop if already at 480 mg. Third event: permanently discontinue. Confirm recurrence/current dose.

rules.explanation: Other intolerable grade 2 or grade 3 toxicity: interrupt until grade 0–1. First event: reference restart 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg if already reduced. Second event: 480 mg twice daily, or stop if already at 480 mg. Third event: permanently discontinue. Confirm recurrence/current dose.

action.message: Third occurrence/persistence after two reductions of intolerable grade 2/grade 3 toxicity requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Third occurrence/persistence after two reductions of intolerable grade 2/grade 3 toxicity requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation.

action.message: The second intolerable grade 2/grade 3 event at an existing 480 mg twice-daily dose requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: The second intolerable grade 2/grade 3 event at an existing 480 mg twice-daily dose requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: Grade 4 first occurrence: consultant chooses permanent discontinuation OR interruption until grade 0–1 with reference restart at 480 mg twice daily; stop if already at 480 mg. This is not an automatic restart decision.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 first occurrence: consultant chooses permanent discontinuation OR interruption until grade 0–1 with reference restart at 480 mg twice daily; stop if already at 480 mg. This is not an automatic restart decision.

action.message: Second grade 4 occurrence/persistence after first reduction requires permanent discontinuation; recovery cannot erase the episode history.

rules.explanation: Second grade 4 occurrence/persistence after first reduction requires permanent discontinuation; recovery cannot erase the episode history.

action.message: Grade 4 toxicity when vemurafenib is already 480 mg twice daily requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 toxicity when vemurafenib is already 480 mg twice daily requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: In this combination source, further reduction after 480 mg twice daily requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: In this combination source, further reduction after 480 mg twice daily requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation.

action.message: Concomitant QT-prolonging drugs are an exclusion in this combination source; reconcile the medicine list before proceeding.

rules.explanation: Concomitant QT-prolonging drugs are an exclusion in this combination source; reconcile the medicine list before proceeding.

action.message: Baseline eligibility requires LVEF >50%; exactly 50% does not meet that entry criterion. Reconcile before starting.

rules.explanation: Baseline eligibility requires LVEF >50%; exactly 50% does not meet that entry criterion. Reconcile before starting.

action.message: Distinguish baseline eligibility (>50%) from on-treatment criteria before interpreting this LVEF.

rules.explanation: Distinguish baseline eligibility (>50%) from on-treatment criteria before interpreting this LVEF.

action.message: Record baseline LVEF and symptoms. On-treatment 40–49% is not an automatic hold without considering the ≥10-point decline and symptoms.

rules.explanation: Record baseline LVEF and symptoms. On-treatment 40–49% is not an automatic hold without considering the ≥10-point decline and symptoms.

action.message: Asymptomatic LVEF <40%, or 40–49% with ≥10-point absolute fall: interrupt cobimetinib for two weeks and reassess. Vemurafenib is assessed independently.

rules.explanation: Asymptomatic LVEF <40%, or 40–49% with ≥10-point absolute fall: interrupt cobimetinib for two weeks and reassess. Vemurafenib is assessed independently.

action.message: Symptomatic LV dysfunction: interrupt cobimetinib for four weeks and reassess. If symptoms attributed to cobimetinib fail to improve, consider permanent cessation.

rules.explanation: Symptomatic LV dysfunction: interrupt cobimetinib for four weeks and reassess. If symptoms attributed to cobimetinib fail to improve, consider permanent cessation.

action.message: The source specifies a 2-week cobimetinib interruption before this cardiac reassessment.

rules.explanation: The source specifies a 2-week cobimetinib interruption before this cardiac reassessment.

action.message: Persistent ≥10-point LVEF decline after the specified cardiac interruption requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Persistent ≥10-point LVEF decline after the specified cardiac interruption requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

action.message: The source specifies a 4-week cobimetinib interruption before this cardiac reassessment.

rules.explanation: The source specifies a 4-week cobimetinib interruption before this cardiac reassessment.

action.message: Persistent ≥10-point LVEF decline after the specified cardiac interruption requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Persistent ≥10-point LVEF decline after the specified cardiac interruption requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

action.message: Persistent cardiac symptoms after the four-week interruption require permanent cobimetinib discontinuation regardless of LVEF.

rules.explanation: Persistent cardiac symptoms after the four-week interruption require permanent cobimetinib discontinuation regardless of LVEF.

action.message: SOURCE OVERLAP: LVEF <40% meets the permanent-stop row while a <10-point decline appears in the restart row. Do not automatically restart or calculate a dose; obtain specialist interpretation and keep cobimetinib withheld.

rules.explanation: SOURCE OVERLAP: LVEF <40% meets the permanent-stop row while a <10-point decline appears in the restart row. Do not automatically restart or calculate a dose; obtain specialist interpretation and keep cobimetinib withheld.

action.message: A third cardiac occurrence requiring interruption/reduction reaches the source permanent-discontinuation step; current recovery does not remove the history.

rules.explanation: A third cardiac occurrence requiring interruption/reduction reaches the source permanent-discontinuation step; current recovery does not remove the history.

action.message: After the required interruption and clinical reassessment, reference cardiac restart doses are cobimetinib 40 mg daily for the first occurrence and 20 mg for the second; third occurrence means permanent cessation. Confirm timing/current dose and specialist approval.

rules.explanation: After the required interruption and clinical reassessment, reference cardiac restart doses are cobimetinib 40 mg daily for the first occurrence and 20 mg for the second; third occurrence means permanent cessation. Confirm timing/current dose and specialist approval.

action.message: Interrupt cobimetinib for rhabdomyolysis or symptomatic CPK elevation. Vemurafenib may continue if clinically appropriate; no blanket numerical CK ≥5×ULN whole-regimen rule applies.

rules.explanation: Interrupt cobimetinib for rhabdomyolysis or symptomatic CPK elevation. Vemurafenib may continue if clinically appropriate; no blanket numerical CK ≥5×ULN whole-regimen rule applies.

action.message: Asymptomatic grade 4 CPK elevation: interrupt cobimetinib. If CPK does not improve to grade ≤3 within four weeks, permanently discontinue.

rules.explanation: Asymptomatic grade 4 CPK elevation: interrupt cobimetinib. If CPK does not improve to grade ≤3 within four weeks, permanently discontinue.

action.message: Asymptomatic CPK grade ≤3 with rhabdomyolysis excluded does not require cobimetinib modification. Other domains remain separately assessed.

rules.explanation: Asymptomatic CPK grade ≤3 with rhabdomyolysis excluded does not require cobimetinib modification. Other domains remain separately assessed.

action.message: Confirm muscle symptoms and exclusion of rhabdomyolysis before choosing the CPK pathway.

rules.explanation: Confirm muscle symptoms and exclusion of rhabdomyolysis before choosing the CPK pathway.

action.message: The interrupted CPK/rhabdomyolysis event did not reach its source recovery threshold within four weeks. Permanently discontinue cobimetinib; later symptom/CPK improvement does not erase the missed deadline.

rules.explanation: The interrupted CPK/rhabdomyolysis event did not reach its source recovery threshold within four weeks. Permanently discontinue cobimetinib; later symptom/CPK improvement does not erase the missed deadline.

action.message: Symptomatic CPK/rhabdomyolysis without at least one-grade improvement within four weeks requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Symptomatic CPK/rhabdomyolysis without at least one-grade improvement within four weeks requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

action.message: If symptomatic CPK/rhabdomyolysis improves by at least one grade within four weeks, cobimetinib may restart 20 mg lower if clinically indicated, with close monitoring.

rules.explanation: If symptomatic CPK/rhabdomyolysis improves by at least one grade within four weeks, cobimetinib may restart 20 mg lower if clinically indicated, with close monitoring.

action.message: Asymptomatic grade 4 CPK that has not improved to grade ≤3 within four weeks requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Asymptomatic grade 4 CPK that has not improved to grade ≤3 within four weeks requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

action.message: After asymptomatic grade 4 CPK improves to grade ≤3 within four weeks, consider cobimetinib restart 20 mg lower with close monitoring. Confirm the actual time to recovery.

rules.explanation: After asymptomatic grade 4 CPK improves to grade ≤3 within four weeks, consider cobimetinib restart 20 mg lower with close monitoring. Confirm the actual time to recovery.

action.message: Current EMA Cotellic: withhold cobimetinib for diagnosed serous retinopathy until visual symptoms improve to grade ≤1; obtain ophthalmic assessment and consultant dose review.

rules.explanation: Current EMA Cotellic: withhold cobimetinib for diagnosed serous retinopathy until visual symptoms improve to grade ≤1; obtain ophthalmic assessment and consultant dose review.

action.message: Interrupt cobimetinib during assessment of grade 3, grade 4 or cerebral bleeding. For grade 4/cerebral events attributed to cobimetinib, permanently discontinue. Vemurafenib may continue if clinically indicated.

rules.explanation: Interrupt cobimetinib during assessment of grade 3, grade 4 or cerebral bleeding. For grade 4/cerebral events attributed to cobimetinib, permanently discontinue. Vemurafenib may continue if clinically indicated.

action.message: Grade 4 or cerebral haemorrhage attributed to cobimetinib requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 or cerebral haemorrhage attributed to cobimetinib requires permanent cobimetinib discontinuation.

action.message: Grade 1–2 liver laboratory toxicity: continue the prescribed cobimetinib/vemurafenib doses while monitoring; this is not overall treatment clearance.

rules.explanation: Grade 1–2 liver laboratory toxicity: continue the prescribed cobimetinib/vemurafenib doses while monitoring; this is not overall treatment clearance.

action.message: Grade 3 liver laboratory toxicity: hold vemurafenib; once grade ≤1, restart one dose level lower after review. Cobimetinib continues at its prescribed dose if otherwise appropriate.

rules.explanation: Grade 3 liver laboratory toxicity: hold vemurafenib; once grade ≤1, restart one dose level lower after review. Cobimetinib continues at its prescribed dose if otherwise appropriate.

action.message: Grade 4 liver laboratory toxicity: interrupt BOTH drugs. If recovery to grade ≤1 occurs within four weeks, source restart reduces cobimetinib by one level and vemurafenib by two levels, subject to current-dose/minimum-dose review.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 liver laboratory toxicity: interrupt BOTH drugs. If recovery to grade ≤1 occurs within four weeks, source restart reduces cobimetinib by one level and vemurafenib by two levels, subject to current-dose/minimum-dose review.

action.message: Recurrent grade 4 liver abnormalities after initial improvement require discontinuation of both cobimetinib and vemurafenib; current improvement does not remove this history.

rules.explanation: Recurrent grade 4 liver abnormalities after initial improvement require discontinuation of both cobimetinib and vemurafenib; current improvement does not remove this history.

action.message: Grade 4 liver toxicity that did not resolve to grade ≤1 within four weeks requires discontinuation of both drugs, even if it subsequently improved.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 liver toxicity that did not resolve to grade ≤1 within four weeks requires discontinuation of both drugs, even if it subsequently improved.

action.message: At four weeks after interruption, persistent liver toxicity above grade 1 following a grade 4 event meets the source discontinuation criterion for both drugs.

rules.explanation: At four weeks after interruption, persistent liver toxicity above grade 1 following a grade 4 event meets the source discontinuation criterion for both drugs.

action.message: First grade 4 liver event recovered to grade ≤1 within four weeks: confirm cobimetinib one-level and vemurafenib two-level reduction, existing dose levels and no recurrence. Do not calculate a dose below the permitted minimum.

rules.explanation: First grade 4 liver event recovered to grade ≤1 within four weeks: confirm cobimetinib one-level and vemurafenib two-level reduction, existing dose levels and no recurrence. Do not calculate a dose below the permitted minimum.

action.message: Interrupt both drugs until photosensitivity resolves to grade ≤1. Cobimetinib may restart unchanged; vemurafenib reduction follows the source adverse-event table. Do not impose an automatic cobimetinib reduction.

rules.explanation: Interrupt both drugs until photosensitivity resolves to grade ≤1. Cobimetinib may restart unchanged; vemurafenib reduction follows the source adverse-event table. Do not impose an automatic cobimetinib reduction.

action.message: Intolerable grade 2/grade ≥3 acneiform rash: use cobimetinib general interruption/reduction guidance. Vemurafenib may continue if clinically indicated.

rules.explanation: Intolerable grade 2/grade ≥3 acneiform rash: use cobimetinib general interruption/reduction guidance. Vemurafenib may continue if clinically indicated.

action.message: Intolerable grade 2/grade ≥3 non-acneiform/maculo-papular rash: vemurafenib may be interrupted/reduced per its table. Cobimetinib may continue unchanged if clinically indicated.

rules.explanation: Intolerable grade 2/grade ≥3 non-acneiform/maculo-papular rash: vemurafenib may be interrupted/reduced per its table. Cobimetinib may continue unchanged if clinically indicated.

action.message: Confirm rash phenotype before attributing a component dose change; acneiform and non-acneiform pathways differ.

rules.explanation: Confirm rash phenotype before attributing a component dose change; acneiform and non-acneiform pathways differ.

action.message: Grade ≥3 diarrhoea despite supportive care: hold both drugs until grade ≤1. Recurrent diarrhoea requires reduction of both components after recovery.

rules.explanation: Grade ≥3 diarrhoea despite supportive care: hold both drugs until grade ≤1. Recurrent diarrhoea requires reduction of both components after recovery.

action.message: Recurrent diarrhoea: confirm prior grade/supportive care and recovery, then reduce both doses as clinically indicated. No automatic restart dose is calculated.

rules.explanation: Recurrent diarrhoea: confirm prior grade/supportive care and recovery, then reduce both doses as clinically indicated. No automatic restart dose is calculated.

action.message: Urgently assess severe diarrhoea and confirm response to supportive care before applying the source dose-modification pathway.

rules.explanation: Urgently assess severe diarrhoea and confirm response to supportive care before applying the source dose-modification pathway.

action.message: Cobimetinib: intolerable grade 2/grade 3 or first grade 4 event requires interruption until grade ≤1. Reference restart: 40 mg daily first event, 20 mg second event; third occurrence means CONSIDER permanent discontinuation.

action.message: Third cobimetinib adverse-event occurrence: consider permanent discontinuation with the consultant. The table does not mandate the same automatic stop wording as vemurafenib.

eligibility: Adult unresectable/metastatic melanoma with validated BRAF V600 mutation
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
Regimen-specific exclusions encoded in the assessment

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Highest emetogenic active component and current NCCP classification.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
supportive_care.source_audit_note: Vemurafenib monotherapy: minimal emetogenic potential; dabrafenib and cobimetinib/vemurafenib: minimal-to-low. Premedication not usually required; antiemetics per local policy. No default prophylactic medicines prescribed.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile; LDH
ECG and LVEF assessment; baseline eligibility LVEF >50%
during: FBC, renal and liver profile and LDH before each 28-day cycle
ECG every four weeks for twelve weeks, then every twelve weeks and after dose modification
After a reduced-dose cobimetinib restart: LVEF approximately two, four, ten and sixteen weeks, then as clinically indicated
Severe hepatic impairment: vemurafenib liver biochemistry twice weekly
Review cardiac, visual, bleeding, muscle, skin and gastrointestinal symptoms; additional tests follow the relevant source/SmPC and clinical plan
after: Contraception advice requires both component SmPCs: NCCP combination text specifies two effective methods for cobimetinib and three months after; vemurafenib monotherapy NCCP specifies six months. Confirm the longer component requirement rather than shortening it.
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Consultant treatment plan; no universal imaging or tumour-marker interval is specified.
smPC_supplement: EMA Zelboraf: ECG/electrolytes including magnesium in ALL patients before treatment, after one month and after dose modification (NCCP00102 baseline wording says at-risk only).
EMA Zelboraf: prescriber skin examination monthly during treatment and up to six months afterwards; reconcile with NCCP00102 week 8 then q12-week dermatology schedule.
EMA Zelboraf: head/neck baseline and every 3 months, chest CT baseline and every 6 months for secondary malignancy surveillance; anal/pelvic examination before/end treatment when indicated.
EMA Cotellic: LVEF baseline, after the first month, then at least every three months until cessation; separate reduced-dose restart schedule remains 2, 4, 10 and 16 weeks.
EMA Cotellic: CPK and creatinine baseline, then monthly or as clinically indicated; visual symptoms assessed at each visit.
